title: Divide Sewing Lines Based on Notches
content: **Divide Sewing Lines Based On Nothches_ver.4.1.0** \- Now sewing lines can be created snapping on notches, without adding segment points. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022653788/mceclip0.png)**Segment Sewing** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Establish sewing lines based on notches.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the Segment Sewing tool to create sewing lines by snapping to notches, streamlining the sewing process in version 4.1.0.

title: Edit Notch Properties
content: **List of Contents** Notch Properties Edit Notch Properties Notch Length **Notch Properties ** \- Edit properties of a Notch as needed. \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026559547/mceclip0.png) **Notch** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Edit Notch Properties ** \- Select the Notch to be modified. \- The properties of the selected Notch appear in the Property Editor. * **Name **\- Rename the Notch. * **Type ** \- Choose the type of the Notch. * **Angle ** \- Set the degree of angle for the Notch. * **Perpendicular** \- The Notch is placed perpendicular to its segment. * **Custom** \- Decide the angle of the Notch based on its segment. * **Direction ** \- This option only appears when a Notch is created in a corner. \- Decided the direction of the Notch. * **Point (Center)** \- The Notch is created at the center of the corner. * **Segment 1** \- The Notch is created towards a segment. * **Segment 2** \- The Notch is created towards the other segment. * **Flip ** \- The Notch is created on the other side of the segment. **Notch Length_ver.5.0.0 and Above** \- Edit Notch length as desired. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing and customizing notch properties and lengths in the design software.

content: **List of Contents** Select Move **Objective** Select or move notches. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![notch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024295548/notch.png) **Notch** ** Operation** **Select** 1. title: Notch
content: **List of Contents** Notch Create Notch Select Notch Move Notch Delete Notch Notch on Seam Allowance Notch Display Type **Notch ** \- Create, select, move, and delete Notches on Pattern outlines. \- Select the Notch tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** ** Create Notch** * **Create Manually ** \- Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline or Internal Line where a notch should be added. \- A red point appears on the segment where the mouse is hovering over. \- Click on the segment to create a Notch and it is automatically selected and highlighted in yellow. * **Create with Specific Numbers ** \- To create a Notch on a specific position, right click on a segment where a notch is desired to be added. \- The Notch window appears allowing you to specify location. * **Split into Two Lines ** \- The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as **Line 1** , and the longer side is indicated as **Line 2.** \- The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. * **Split by Length** \- Divide the selected line into multiple segments according to the desired length of each segment. \- **Segment Length** : Enter the segment length, which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select Reverse Direction. \- **Number of Segments** : Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. \- **Direction** : Reverse the direction that points are added. * **Uniform Split** \- Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into next to the **Number of Segments** option. The line is equally divided accordingly. **Select Notch ** \- Click the Notch created on a segment. \- The Notch is selected and highlighted in yellow. **Move Notch** * **Move Manually ** \- Click and drag the Notch created on a Pattern outline or an Internal Line. \- Release the mouse when the Notch is moved to the desired place. \- The Notch is successfully moved. * **Move with Specific Numbers ** \- To move the Notch with specific numbers, right click while click-and-dragging the Notch. \- Enter the desired value when the Moving Distance window appears. 。 \- The Notch is moved accordingly. **Delete Notch ** \- Select the Notch to be deleted. \- Hit the Delete key on the keyboard. \- Or, right click on the Notch to be deleted and select Delete option from the pop-up menu. **Notch on Seam Allowance_ver5.0.0 and Above ** \- When a notch is added, it appears on both its Pattern Outline and the seam allowance. \- When a seam allowance is added to a Pattern Outline with a notch, the notch appears on the seam allowance as well. \- When a notch is added to a corner with seam allowance, the notch randomly appears on either side of the seam allowance at the corner. **Notch Display Type_ver5.0.0 and Above ** \- Configure notches' 2D display options. \- Navigate to the path: Main Menu ▶ Setting ▶ User Setting ▶ 2Dㅁ ▶ **Notch** * **Length Fixed to Screen** : Notches are displayed in a fixed length regardless of the screen size (zoom in or out.) ※Note: When this option is selected, the **Notch Length** option disappears from the Property Editor. * **Actual Length** : Notches's size adapts to the screen size (zoom in or out.) ※Note : When this option is selected, the Notch Length option appears in the Property Editor. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create, select, move, and delete notches on pattern outlines, along with options for notch display and functionality related to seam allowances.

title: Create Notch
content: **List of Contents** Create Manually Create with Specific Values Add Point to Notch **Objective** Create notch on Pattern outlines as desired to improve sewing accuracy. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Notch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![notch.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024295408/notch.png) **Notch** **Operation** **Create Manually** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Hover the mouse over the Pattern outline where the notch is to be added. → A notch is created and the [notch properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013369268-Edit-Notch-Properties) appear in the Property Editor. **※Note:** Right-click on a point with Edit Pattern or Edit Curve Point tool (ver 6.1) and click Add Notch, a notch is created at the point **Create with Specific Values ** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right-click on the Pattern outline where notches should be added to access the pop-up window. Then, type in the desired values referring to the table below. ****** ****** **Split Into Two Lines** | Line 1 / Line 2 | The line will be divided into two lines based on the reference point which was created when you hover the mouse over and right click the segment. The shorter side is indicated as Line 1, and the longer side is indicated as Line 2. Enter the desired value in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. ---|---|--- Ratio | The ratio of the line to be split is 100%. The line can be divided into two lines based on the ratio. Enter the desired ratio in either Line 1 or Line 2 to split the segment into two lines. This function is often used split a line into two identical segments or to add a point at its 33.3%. **Split by Length** **** | Segment Length | Enter the segment length which the whole line should be divided according to the interval. To reverse the direction that points are added, select **Reverse Direction**. Number of Segments | Enter the number of segments the selected line should be divided into. It is set as 2 by default. Direction | Reverse the direction that points are added. **Uniform Split** | Enter the number of segments the line should be divided into. The line is equally divided accordingly. 3. The notches are created based on the chosen options. **Add Point to Notch** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the notch and click Add Point to Notch. → A straight point is added to the notch. **※Note:** If there is a seam allowance in the pattern in which the notch was created, the notch also appears in the seam allowance. In addition, if a notch is created in the corner of a pattern with seam allowance, the notch appears randomly only in one seam allowance of both seams. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to create notches on pattern outlines in CLO 3D to enhance sewing accuracy, including manual creation, specific value settings, and adding points to notches.

title: Internal Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Internal Ellipse Create **Internal Ellipse ** \- Create ellipse or circle within a Pattern. \- Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001203908/Toolbar_2D_Shape_Inner_Circle.png)**Internal Ellipse** **Create** * **Create**** ** \- Click and drag within a Pattern to create an ellipse in the 2D window. \- To create a circle, hold down the Shift key while click and drag. * **Create with Specific Values** \- Click within a Pattern to create an ellipse with specific values. \- The Create Ellipse window appears. * Size Diameter: Set width and height of an ellipse. Radius: Set width and height of the radius of an ellipse. Circumference: Set overall circumference of an ellipse. * Replicate Interval : Set the distance between each replicated ellipses. Angle : Set the angle between each replicated ellipses. Number of Shapes : Set the number of ellipses to be replicated. * Position Outline : Configure the ellipse’s location by setting the ellipse outline’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Center : Configure the ellipse’s location by setting the ellipse center’s offset from the Pattern outlines’ left, right, top, and bottom. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for creating and customizing internal ellipses or circles within a pattern using the 2D design tools.

title: Create Custom Texture Image
content: **List of Contents** Scan Fabric Create Repeat Match DPI (Resolution) Match Color **Objective** Create various custom texture images and apply to fabrics to express variety of fabric in CLO. There are four steps total to create a custom texture image: Scanning Fabric, Making Repeat, Matching DPI (Resolution), and Adjusting Color. In order to make custom texture image, image editing software, such as [Pixplant](https://www.pixplant.com/index.php), [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) is needed. **Operation** **Scan Fabric** Scan fabrics to digitize real world fabrics. If scanner is not available, use digital camera or cellphone camera instead. 1. Prepare the scanner, digital camera, or cellphone camera. 2. Spread the fabric flat on an even surface and photograph it, aligning the grainline perpendicular to the scanner or the camera's corner of the screen. 3. Send the image to the computer. **Create Repeat ** When a fabric is observed carefully, you can find the structure which repeats like a pattern and the structure of the fabric is often indicated as a Repeat. To express a fabric's texture, create a Repeat using the scanned image. Ways to create a Repeat differs depending on the characteristics of each fabric. Please refer to the appropriate guideline as needed. **When Fabric Structure is Small and Irregular** 1. Launch [PixPlant](https://www.pixplant.com/download.php). If PixPlant is not available, please use other image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop. 2. Left click on the Add button on the right top corner and locate the scanned image to load. 3. Left click on the Straighten Seed > Click to Edit button, then select a clean part of the scanned image. 4. Click the Generate button to create a Repeat. 5. The area inside the square box in the Texture Canvas window represents the Repeat. Repeat procedure 3 and 4 until the desired Repeat is achieved. 6. To recreate some portion of the Repeat, drag to select the desired part within the square box in the Texture Canvas window. 7. When the desired Repeat is achieved, click Save. **When Fabric Structure is Big and Regular** 1. Launch [Adobe Photoshop](http://www.adobe.com/products/photoshop.html) or other image editing software. 2. Find the smallest repeated area on the scanned image. 3. Select and cut the repeated area. 4. Copy, paste and align repeated area to check if they align naturally. 5. When the repeated area does not align properly, showing grid lines, edit the image to make it align more smoothly. 6. When the desired image is achieved, save the image. **※ Note:** When creating Repeats for fabrics with transparency, please select and delete the Repeat image's background and save it as PNG. **Match DPI (Resolution)** In order to match the image ratio of the Repeat and the real world fabric, adjust DPI (Resolution). 1. Launch Adobe Photoshop. 2. Open previously created Repeat. 3. Navigate and select Main Menu > Image > Image Size. 4. When a pop-up window appears, toggle on the Resample Image option and adjust the DPI (Resoultion) value respective to the DPI (Resolution) of the original scanned image. Open the original scanned image in Adobe Photoshop to check its DPI (Resolution) value. 5. Save the Repeat. **Match Color** Match the Repeat's color respective to the real world fabric. Occasionally, photographing fabric may distort the fabric's real color. In these cases, after creating a Repeat image, adjust its color, matching the color to the original fabric's color. Open the Repeat in an image editing software such as Adobe Photoshop and adjust color as needed. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating custom texture images from scanned fabrics, including instructions on scanning, repeating patterns, matching DPI, and adjusting colors to enhance fabric representation in CLO.

title: How can I express embroidery in CLO?
content: **Question** How can I express embroidery in CLO? **Answer** There are three possible ways to express embroidery in CLO differ by the purpose and the situation. With Scanned Embroidery Without Scanned Embroidery** ** **With Scanned Embroidery** When there is a scanned image of embroidery, use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) in CLO to express embroidery. However, as expressing thick embroidery and flat embroidery methods are different, please refer to the appropriate guide below. ** Express Embroidery with Thickness ** To express embroidery with thickness, please refer to below instruction. 1. [Create](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000511208) a rectangle Pattern in the 2D window. 2. Apply a new fabric to the Pattern and add texture. 3. [Create Internal Lines](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000481707) in the shape of embroidery on the Pattern and cut. 4. Delete unnecessary Pattern and duplicate the Pattern outline as an Internal Shape to the 3D Garment Pattern. 5. [Sew](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000641848-%EC%9E%AC%EB%B4%89%EC%84%A0-%EC%83%9D%EC%84%B1) the embroidery Pattern to the 3D Garment. 6. Click on the fabric item applied to the embroidery Pattern in the Object Browser and change its Preset as Fusible Rigid. Also, change the Particle Distance to 5. ** Express Flat Embroidery ** Use the [Graphic tools](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000483967) to add the embroidery image to the 3D Garment in order to express embroidery with no thickness. **Without Scanned Embroidery **** **If there is no scanned image of embroidery, use the image editing tool such as Adobe Photoshop to express embroidery effects. Then, refer to guides from the With Scanned Embroidery section. You may search how to express embroidery in image editing tools online or take a look at the reference we found below! [Video Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HbZac9imfZA) Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Discover how to effectively express embroidery in CLO using scanned images or graphic tools, with step-by-step instructions for both thick and flat embroidery techniques.

title: Create Custom Texture Image for Curved Pattern
content: **List of Contents** Using Adobe Photoshop Using Adobe Illustrator **Objective** Create custom texture image for curved pattern such as neckband. Use curved texture image when expressing lace or biz trims. **Operation** **Using Adobe Photoshop ** Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Photoshop. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Photoshop and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Place the Repeat image on top of the pattern image. 7. Use the [Warp](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/warp-images-shapes-paths.html) function to transform the Repeat image respective to the pattern. 8. Open a new window in Adobe Photoshop. 9. Select, copy, and paste the modified Repeat image to the newly opened window. 10. Save the modified Repeat image as PNG and be mindful to set the canvas size bigger than the modified Repeat image for easy application and modification in CLO. 11. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. **Using Adobe Illustrator ** **** Create custom texture image for curved pattern in Adobe Illustrator. 1. [Create a Repeat](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115012228067) of real world fabric. 2. Open the pattern file which the custom texture image will be applied to. 3. Right click on the curved pattern which the custom texture image will be applied to, then select Zoom to Selected on the pop-up menu. 4. Take a screenshot of the pattern. 5. Launch Adobe Illustrator and open both screenshot and Repeat image. 6. Trace the pattern image with the [pen](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/drawing-pen-curvature-or-pencil.html) tool. 7. Select the Repeat image and [add as a pattern brush](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/how-to/illustrator-create-pattern-brush.html). 8. Select and copy the longest segment of the traced pattern and apply the pattern brush created in procedure 6. 9. Place the traced pattern on top of the segment with pattern brush applied. 10. Select both pattern and segment, right click and select Make Clipping Mask. The segment with pattern brush applied will be clipped based on the pattern shape. 11. Select the clipped pattern, navigate and select Main Menu > File > Export Selection. 12. Designate the saving path, file name and save as PNG. 13. [Apply](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000471388) the modified Repeat image to the pattern and [adjust](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002680348) as needed to place the graphic properly. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for creating custom texture images for curved patterns, utilizing both Adobe Photoshop and Adobe Illustrator to enhance fabric design projects.

title: Edit Sewing
content: **List of Contents** **Move** **Properties** **Objective** Select and move Sewing Lines or set properties. ** ****Location** Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶**Edit Sewing (B)** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33928598651417) **Edit Sewing (B)** **Operation** **Move** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click the point or segment of Sewing Line ▶Drag it. Or, right click to enter the Distance Moved while moving. **Properties** 1. Click the Sewing Line and set the properties. **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Sewing Line Type** | **Custom Angle**** **| Set the Angle and Strength of Sewing Line. **Fold Angle** | **** 180° represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. **Fold Strength** | **** The intensity of the fold is able to be set by adjusting the value of Fold Strength. The higher the value, the closer the fold is to the set angle. When a jacket and its lining are sewn together, the sewn area inflates due to the default sewing angle and intensity values. In this case, sets the Fold Strength to 0 to flatten the sewn boundaries. **Turned** | Sew two layers of pattern flatly. After selecting sewing lines, press the**`** key on the keyboard to immediately switch the Sewing Line Type. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/13401097127321) If it is set to Turned, it is not able to adjust the Fold Angle/Strength. **Tension** | When the 3D garment is expressed as being stretched more than the actual garment, adjust the Tension of Sewing Line. Same as actual concept, Tension is applied based on the short or long side with the Ease and Stretch options. **Strength** | Increase or decrease the strength of the sewing tension by entering the value. The result may vary depending on the Strength even with the same Ratio value. **Ratio** | Adjust the sewing tension's ratio to express varying drape effects by different sewing methods. **Set Sublayer**** **| Assign orders to the Sewing Lines on a Pattern which folds on itself such as seam allowances and pleats in order to increase simulation stability. **Reverse Direction** | Swap the fixed Sewing Line and the moving Sewing Line. **Sublayer** | Decide which side of the fabric is attached to the fixed Sewing Line. **Topstitch/ Puckering (ver 7.3[![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/33928646140697)](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=p0je5NkyY58c2i7w&t=2792)) ** | Applying the [Topstitch](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002752908-Edit-Topstitch) and [Puckering](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000617208--Property-Edit-Puckering-Properties) to the seam lines to create a variety of seam lines. You can save a sewing line with the properties applied and easily apply it to other sewing lines. **3D Seamline**** **| Set the direction of seam allowance. **Normal Map** | Select an image to be used as the Normal Map. **Intensity/ Thickness** | Adjust the intensity and thickness of the Normal Map applied to the seamline.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for selecting, moving, and adjusting properties of sewing lines in the garment design software, enabling users to refine their sewing techniques for improved simulation and visual effects.

title: Garment Rendering Style
content: **List of Contents** Garment Rendering Style Textured Surface Thick Textured Surface Transparent Surface Monochrome Surface Mesh Random Colored Surface **Garment Rendering Style** \- Check the tightness of 3D Garments with the color scale. \- Hover over the third icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu in the 3D window. ** Textured Surface** \- Only the front side of the 3D Garment will appear in its original color and the back side will appear darker to indicate the sides of the fabric. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Thick Textured Surface** \- Both front and back sides of the 3D Garment will appear in their original color and the Garment thickness will be expressed. **Transparent Surface** \- The 3D Garment will turn translucent. **Monochrome Surface** \- The 3D Garment will appear in black and white. \- The Garment thickness will not be expressed. **Mesh** \- The 3D Garment will appear in the mesh structure. **Random Color Surface_ver5.0.0 and Above** \- Select the **Random Color Surface** icon to distinguish Patterns as they are assigned to random colors. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore various garment rendering styles to visualize and assess the 3D representation of fabrics with detailed texture and color options.

title: Edit Fabric (Print Layout Mode)

Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ **Edit Texture ** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_texture.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024350388/edit_texture.png) **Edit Texture** ** ** 3. content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for editing fabric textures and roll widths in Print Layout mode within the CLO 3D software.

title: Fabric_Color
content: **List of Contents** Color Change color Change color with Eyedropper **Color** \- Change the color of the fabric. ** Change Color** \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window to assign the desired Color to the selected item. \- Click the desired Color. The selected Color will be applied to the item. \- Click OK to complete. **Change Color with Eyedropper** \- When changing the Color, select the desired item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches. The selected item’s properties will appear in the Property Editor. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and locate the Color chip next to the Color option, under the Material section. \- Click on the Color chip to open the Color window. \- Select the **Eyedropper** tool. \- Drag the mouse cursor outside the Color window. When the cursor changes to an Eyedropper, click on the spot anywhere in the window to extract the desired color. \- The color of the selected spot will appear in the Color window. \- Select OK to complete. \- The chosen Color will be assigned to the selected item. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for changing colors of various design elements using a color selection tool and an eyedropper feature.

title: Garment Information
content: **List of Contents** Garment Information Enter Default Garment Information Add Category Reorder Category Delete Category Save Garment Information **Garment Information** \- Easily record and check necessary information for a 3D Garment. \- Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Information ▶**Garment.** **Enter Default Garment Information** \- Information fields such as Style No, Name, Description, Fabric, Colorway and Size appear in the Garment Information window by default. \- Type in appropriate information for each category. \- Toggle on the **Display When Garment File Loads** option to load the Garment Information every the file opens. \- To save the information, click **OK**. **Add Category** \- Click the**![edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736768/edit.png) Edit** button on the right top corner to add more categories. \- When it shifts to the edit mode, click the ![add.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001760867/add.png) **Add** button on the right top corner. \- When the new category is added, select the desired category type with the drop-down menu. \- Click the ![exit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736748/exit.png)**Exit** button to finish editing. **Reorder Category** \- Click the **![edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736768/edit.png)Edit** button on the right top corner to reorder categories. \- When it shifts to the edit mode, click and drag the category to the desired placement. \- The selected category is moved to where the mouse is released. \- Click the ![exit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736748/exit.png)**Exit** button to finish editing. **Delete Category** \- Click the **![edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736768/edit.png)Edit** button on the right top corner to delete categories. When it shifts to the edit mode, click the ![delete.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001760887/delete.png) **Delete** button next to the category to be removed. \- Click the ![exit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736748/exit.png)**Exit** button to finish editing. **Save Garment Information** \- Click the **![edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001736768/edit.png)Edit** button on the right top corner to delete categories. \- Use the ![save.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001760907/save.png) **Save** button on the right top corner to save category list, order, and contents. \- Saved information can be loaded by using the ![open.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001760927/open.png) **Open** button as well. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for managing garment information, including adding, editing, reordering, and deleting categories, as well as saving and loading garment details for efficient 3D garment design.

title: Edit Binding Properties
content: **List of Contents** Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties **Binding Properties ** \- Adjust properties for Binidngs. ** ** \- Select the Select Binding tool from the 3D toolbar. **※****Note:** Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit Binding Properties ** \- When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. \- Select the Binding to be edited. \- Selected Binding’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Name Rename Binding’s name. * Line Length Check Binding’s length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. * Type * Under Express Inside Bindings. * Over Bindings are placed over the Patterns. * Dimension * Width Adjust selected Binding’s width (1~50mm). * Particle Distance Edit selected Binding’s Particle Distance (1~20mm). * Fabric Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. * Topstitch Add Topstitch to the Binding. Only Topstitches in the Topstitch Object Browser appears for the options. * Sewing Line Type Edit Binding’s Sewing Line Type. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to edit binding properties for 3D garments, detailing the tools and options available for customization.

title: Adjust Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
content: ### **Objective** Use the **Weft** , **Warp** and **Shear** intensities to show the resistance against the horizontal, vertical and diagonal elasticity according to the 2D window. Increasing the **Shear** intensity to the same ratio as the **Weft** and **Warp** intensities, is going to express materials that creases easily such as cotton and denim. On the other hand, decreasing the intensity value is going to express more elastic materials such as silk and jersey. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Stretch-Weft** /**Warp** , **Shear** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548088/______.png)
content_description: This web page aims to demonstrate how varying Weft, Warp, and Shear intensities can influence the elasticity and crease resistance of different fabric materials in a 2D window simulation.

title: Edit Binding Properties
content: **List of Contents** Binding Properties Edit Binding Properties **Binding Properties** \- Adjust properties for Binidngs. ** ** \- Select the ![edit_binding.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001829187/edit_binding.jpg)**Select Binding** tool from the 3D toolbar. **※****Note: ** Binding can also be selected with the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit Binding Properties** \- When the Binding tool is selected, the 3D garment turns translucent and segments with Binding appear in grey. \- Select the Binding to be edited. \- Selected Binding’s properties appear in the Property Editor. * Name : Rename Binding’s name. * Type: Place the Binding below or above the Pattern. * Line Length: Check Binding’s length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. * Width (mm): Adjust selected Binding’s width (1~30mm). * Length (%): Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50~200%) (ver5.0.0.) * Length (in): Adjust selected Binding's length with a specific value. When adjusting the Binding with a specific value, the unit follows the program's default unit (ver5.0.0.) * Particle Distance (mm): Edit selected Binding’s Particle Distance (1~20mm). * Add'l Thickness - Collision (mm): Adjust the **Add'l Thickness - Collision** value of each Binding (ver5.0.0.) * Fabric: Assign Fabric to the Binding. * Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. * Topstitch: Apply Topstitch on top of the Binding. All Topstitch styles added in the Object Browser appear as options (ver4.2.0.) * Sewing Line Type: Edit Binding’s Sewing Line Type. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for adjusting and editing the properties of bindings in garment design, providing step-by-step instructions and essential tools for customization.

title: Adjust Friction Coefficient
content: **Objective** Use this function to adjust the friction of Garments. The Friction Coefficient affects the friction between a Garment and another Garment.** Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Friction**** ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005704367/86__________.png)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the friction coefficient of garments to enhance their interaction with each other in the Fabric Property Editor.

title: [Style Property] Apply Topstitch Texture
content: ### Objective Change texture type for Topstitch(es). **※ Note :** Texture can only be applied when the type is selected for Texture in the Property Editor. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005672048/__.png) **Search** **Operation** 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch to add texture image. → The selected Topstitch is now being highlighted. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005672048/__.png) **Search** → The Open File window appears. 3. title: Elastic
content: ### List of Contents Pattern Pattern Outline or Internal Line ### Objective Apply elastic to the patterns or lines to express details such as E-bands or shirring. ### Operation #### **Pattern (ver 7.2)** 1. In the Library window, click Fabric » Elastic folder. 2. In the fabric tab of the Object Browser, select the fabric of the pattern to represent E-band. → Property Editor appears. 3. Click the Elastic option on the right side of the Physical Property. → Elastic properties appear. 4. Adjust the Elastic properties. | Preset | Set the default elastic presets. ---|--- Strength and Stiffness | Adjust the strength and stiffness of the elastic. Thickness | Set the thickness of the elastic. #### **Pattern Outline or Internal Line** 1. Select a outer or internal line with ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005538548/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** tool. → Property Editor appears. 2. Click the Elastic option to **On**. 3. Adjust the Elastic properties. Strength | Adjust the strength of the elastic. ---|--- Ratio | Adjust the ratio of the elastic. Segment Length | Adjusts the elastic ratio when the length value is entered. Total Length | If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for applying elastic properties to patterns and lines in fabric design, detailing step-by-step instructions and adjustable parameters for optimal customization.

title: Opacity
content: **Opacity** \- Adjust the **Opacity** to express see-through materials. \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and adjust Material ▶ **Opacity.** \- Adjust the scrollbar or type in desired values to edit the Opacity values. \- The material’s Opacity will change according to the setting.
content_description: This webpage provides a guide on how to adjust the opacity of materials to create see-through effects using the Object Browser and Property Editor.

title: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
content: ### **Objective** Use **Bending** intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately likewise the real fabrics. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Bending-Weft** /**Warp** **Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548248/________01.png) **Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548268/________02.png) **※Note:** Adjust Bending for bias by using **Bending - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the bending intensity of fabric to control stiffness, allowing users to customize the properties of both weft and warp directions for various materials.

title: Open Textures in AI / PS (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Open the texture image applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop. ### **Location** Fabric Property ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900008317346/mceclip0.png) button right to each map. ### **Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The pop-up menu appears. 2. Click Add Another App menu. → Select Application window appears. 3. Select the executable file (EXE) of the application to be added. Click Open button. → The texture will then open in that application and the application will be added to the list of the pop-up menu as well. 4. Save the edited texture in the application, return to CLO, then right-click on the background in the 3D window. ▶ Click **Refresh Textures (F5)**. → The edited texture image appears. **※Note:** * Once you click Open with Another App menu, you can only execute the selected application without adding it to the pop-up menu. * User Settings ▶ [Other](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360001547188-%EA%B8%B0%ED%83%80-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) you can register or delete the application that is opening textures.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for opening and editing texture images applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator or Photoshop within CLO 3D.

title: Adjust Rendering Thickness
content: **List of Contents** Fabric Unit Pattern Unit **Objective** Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as default vale, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. **※ Note: **To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on **Thick Textured Surface** . **Location** **Fabric Unit ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ **Thickness** **Pattern Unit**(ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Rendering** **Operation** **Fabric Unit** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: ** **Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶**Thickness** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. **Pattern Unit**(ver2.3.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Rendering** 2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for setting and adjusting fabric thickness for garments in a 3D environment, ensuring proper rendering visibility.

title: Adjust Buckling Ratio
content: **Objective** Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer the ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Ratio** ![_____________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018758847/_____________.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Ratio for bias by using **Buckling Ratio - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: This webpage provides insights into the Buckling Ratio of fabrics, illustrating how it influences their bendability from flexible materials like silk to stiffer options like denim.

title: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
content: **Objective** Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Stiffness-Weft** /**Warp** ** ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005756128/____.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Stiffness for bias by using **Buckling Stiffness - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a detailed guide for adjusting the percentage of bending intensity to determine the buckling stiffness of fabric corners, facilitating better control over fabric folding behavior in design applications.

title: [Mode] Emulator
content: ### **Objective** Digitize new fabric and save as a file in Emulator Mode. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ **EMULATOR** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Change the mode at the top-right corner ▶ **EMULATOR** → Emulator window appears. 2. Input the property value of the fabric measured step by step according to the description on the left screen. **※ Note:** Select **Enter All Values** to skip to the last page where users may manually enter all values without going through previous steps. (ver 5.1.0) ![emulator.JPG](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360039474014/emulator.JPG) 3. Press **Compute** once finish putting the value and wait until automatic calculation for the fabric property is completed. 4. Save the calculated fabric as .zfab file. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000708348/1.PNG)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for digitizing new fabric and saving it as a .zfab file in Emulator Mode.

title: Select Binding
content: ### **Objective** Edit Binding Properties. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Binding ▶ **Select Binding** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Select Binding ** **※Note:** 3D toolbar ▶ Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated.** **→ The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. 2. Select the Binding to be edited. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Rename Binding's name. **Line Length** | Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. **Type**** ** | **Under** | Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. **Over ** | Bindings are placed over the Patterns. **Both (ver 7.0)** | Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. **Dimension** | **Width** | Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) **Length ** | Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. **Particle Distance** | Edit selected Binding's [Particle Distance](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000414447-Particle-Distance-Setting-) (4~20mm) **Add'l Thickness - Collision** | Adjust Binding's[ Add'l Thickness - Collision](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002798068-Adjust-Collision-Thickness). **Fabric** | Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the [Fabric Object Browser](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/sections/115000714287-FABRIC) appear in a list. **Grain Direction**** ** | Bias/ Warp/ Custom | Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle | Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. **Topstitch ** | Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. [**Sewing Line Type**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000496627--Property-Sewing-Line-Type) | Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. **Extend ** | Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. **※ Note:** Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. 4. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete selected Binding. **Reset Arrangement** | Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. **Deactivate / Activate** | Deactivate or activate selected Binding. **Freeze / Unfreeze** | Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. **Flip Normal ** | The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for editing binding properties in the 3D toolbar, enabling users to customize their designs effectively.

title: Palette
content: **List of Contents** Color Palette Color Swatch Color Palette Palette Library **Color Palette** \- Import Color Palettes from Adobe Illustrator or Adobe Photoshop or create a custom Color Palette to utilize during the design process. ** ****Color Swatch** **** * **Add Color Swatch** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the desired color from the Color Browser window or the Color Swatch Library. \- Click the Add Button. \- The selected color will be added as a swatch. * **Rename Color Swatch** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the **Display** button on the furthest right top of the Color Palette. \- The Color Palette display will change and each color swatch’s name will appear. \- Double click the color name to edit. \- Type in the desired color name and select OK. * **Re-order Color Swatch** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material > **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click and drag the color swatch to be reordered. \- Release the mouse to complete the modification. **Color Palette** **** * **Reset Color Palette** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material > **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022237847/mceclip1.png)**Reset Custom Palette** button on the right top of the Color Palette. \- The dialogue informing that all color swatches will be removed will pop-up. Select **Reset.** \- All color swatches will be deleted from the Color Palette. * **Save Color Palette** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material > **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022313188/mceclip2.png) **Save as Palette** button on the right top of the Color Palette. \- Designate the saving path and file name, and then select **Save.** \- The custom Color Palette will be saved as .aco files. * **Open Color Palette ** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. **-** Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.**** **\- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022238267/mceclip3.png) **Open Palette** button on the right top of the color palette.**** The Open Palette window will pop-up allowing you to choose an option for importing a Color Palette: to delete and create a new Color Palette, click the New button. On the other hand, to add a new Color Palette, select the Add Button. \- Locate the Color Palette file and click Open. \- The desired Color Palette will be loaded. * **Change color Palette Display -** Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶**Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- There are total of three display styles and each change with the click of the Display button on the right top of the Color Palette. **Palette Library** **** * **Create Palette Library** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- Click the **+** button on the right top of the Palette Library. \- The Open File window will pop-up. \- The Open File window will pop-up. \- The selected Palette file will be added to the library as a new tab. * **Copy to Color Palette** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. 。 \- Click the **Copy to Custom Palette** button on the right bottom of the Palette Library. \- The Copy to Custom Palette window will pop-up allowing you to choose an option for importing a Color Palette: to delete and create a new Color Palette, click the New button. On the other hand, to add a new Color Palette, select the Add Button. \- The color swatches in the selected Color Palette will be copied to the Custom Palette. * **Change Color Palette Display ** \- Select an item among Avatars, Fabrics, Buttons, and Topstitches to change its color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and click the color chip next to Material ▶ **Color.** \- The Color window will appear, allowing you to select the color for the item. \- There are total of three display styles and each change with the click of the Display button on the right top of the Color Palette. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing and customizing color palettes and swatches in your design process, including importing, creating, and organizing color options for various design elements.
